title: Mixed-characteristic fibre comparison
as_he_states: Compare the characteristic-p crystalline fibre with a characteristic-zero integral p-adic fibre; the author expects nonisomorphism in general and retains an uncertain finite-field exception, without fixing every structure.
plausible_today: Specify a smooth proper object, a good-reduction model, coefficient rings, Frobenius and filtration, then ask for the appropriate period-ring comparison; no bare canonical Q_p comparison is presumed.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne82 §1 gives Betti/de Rham and étale comparisons; Colmez–Fontaine TheoremA gives rational semistable admissibility, with crystalline subcase N=0. Oda5.11 concerns H¹ and A[p], not this whole mixed-characteristic comparison.
why_open: The pages leave the integral and Frobenius conventions incomplete; the sources do not identify that omission with a single historical open problem.
worth: Worth clarifying the category and coefficients first, because otherwise different valid comparison theorems answer different questions.

title: Compatibility of the real conjugations
as_he_states: Verify the commuting involutions and their product, called real Frobenius, including the l-adic comparison.
plausible_today: For a smooth proper real variety, use the same Betti/de Rham/étale comparison and distinguish scalar conjugation from geometric pullback.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne82 pp7–9 supplies the real comparison setting. D2 proves commutation there; C09 disproves an argument using arbitrary semilinear involutions alone.
why_open: The manuscript explicitly marks the compatibility for verification; this is a normalization check, not a presently open theorem in the geometric setting.
worth: Worth a short convention audit linking all three realizations.

title: The proposed motivic level subspace
as_he_states: The indicated rational intersection of Hodge filtration and real-Frobenius translate is motivic and represents the stated level.
plausible_today: Replace the naive intersection by the largest rational sub-Hodge structure in the specified filtration; algebraicity/coniveau equality is a further generalized Hodge question.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Grothendieck1969 §§1–2 explicitly corrects the naive formulation. D3 and C12 give a dimension-five odd-weight obstruction, also embedded in the real setting. The manuscript index rho still needs an ink check.
why_open: Grothendieck’s later paper explains the elementary defect of the original Hodge-conjecture formulation; no claim is made that this exact leaf already has his corrected definition.
worth: Worth resolving the index and comparing the two formulations before treating it as an open coniveau conjecture.

title: Real and totally real neutralization in characteristic p
as_he_states: For sufficiently large motivic pieces in characteristic p, perhaps T_alpha(R) is empty; ask whether a totally real extension can provide a point.
plausible_today: For a category containing h¹ of a supersingular elliptic curve with all geometric endomorphisms and ordinary dimension-two realizations, no real or totally real neutralization exists.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Voight42.1.9 identifies the geometric quaternion endomorphism algebra; D4 proves it cannot act on R². Deligne–Milne4.17/4.27/4.29 distinguish real fibre functors and polarization conventions.
why_open: The manuscript poses the question; the quaternion obstruction explains the stated large-category obstruction, not the fate of every smaller category.
worth: Worth identifying the minimal tensor subcategory and its precise gerbe, with the Codex Deuring gerbe kept separate until matched.

title: Geometric points versus enriched fibre functors
as_he_states: A suitably enriched transcendental motivic point should correspond bijectively to a complex point modulo conjugation.
plausible_today: Fix the category and integral Hodge/real descent data, then formulate injectivity and essential-image recognition separately.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne–Milne3.2 classifies fibre functors by torsors after a neutralization. Milne6.8 classifies polarizable integral weight-one Hodge structures by complex abelian varieties. Neither classifies all points of an arbitrary X through its proposed motives.
why_open: The pages themselves call for additional structure; the opened sources give no general historical explanation or complete theorem with these quantifiers.
worth: Worth testing a precisely defined abelian or elliptic subcategory before asserting an all-motives correspondence.

title: Characteristic-p points with Witt and F,V data
as_he_states: Revisit the proposed Witt-valued fibre functors and Frobenius/Verschiebung structures characterizing characteristic-p points.
plausible_today: For an abelian variety over a perfect field, use the contravariant Dieudonné module of A[p] to recover H¹_dR with its specified structure; keep the general point-recognition programme separate.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Oda Cor5.11, printed131, gives M(A[p])≅H¹_dR(A). Cor5.12 for smooth proper X over a perfect field with X(k) nonempty gives an injection from DM of the p-kernel of Pic_X, not all H¹. This does not supply an integral motivic essential image.
why_open: The page says Questions and À revoir; the concrete abelian reconstruction was subsequently proved, while the surrounding universal category remains unspecified.
worth: Worth tracing the exact link to cote54/007; avoid treating Oda as a solution to the larger programme.

title: Filtered characteristic-zero points
as_he_states: Characterize characteristic-zero geometric points by filtered fibre functors over the realization field.
plausible_today: State the necessary tensor, polarization, integrality and admissibility conditions for one fixed category, then ask whether they are sufficient.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Hodge theory and Colmez–Fontaine give specific realization categories; Milne6.8–6.9 provides the weight-one integral/rational distinction. None of the opened theorems gives the proposed universal geometric essential image.
why_open: The conditions are not fully stated on the page, so the obstruction is partly one of formulation rather than an identified unsolved theorem.
worth: Worth formulating a sharply bounded recognition problem.

title: Discrete motivic group and topological monodromy
as_he_states: Compare Aut^tensor(xi)=G_xi(Z) with the topological fundamental group when xi comes from a geometric fibre.
plausible_today: A geometric local system gives a monodromy homomorphism into the tensor automorphism group; its kernel, image and closure depend on the tensor category and integral model.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne–Milne tensor reconstruction and Arapura §§6–7 distinguish a Tannakian algebraic envelope from the underlying discrete topological group. No equality of the two groups follows from the notation pi_1.
why_open: The page announces the comparison but supplies no complete category or theorem; no later exact universal equality was verified.
worth: Worth computing the image in one explicit variation, keeping discrete, algebraic and profinite completions distinct.

title: Finiteness of integral fibre functors
as_he_states: For fixed alpha there are finitely many integral fibre functors, by Borel–Harish-Chandra.
plausible_today: Prove a reduction to integral points on finitely many closed rational reductive orbits with fixed lattice, or impose hypotheses that give such a reduction.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Borel–Harish-Chandra Theorem6.9, printed510–511, proves finiteness of arithmetic orbits on a closed orbit in a rational representation. The supplied pages omit the reduction of their integral tensor forms to that situation.
why_open: The manuscript gives only the citation. The published theorem shows exactly where closedness, reductivity and a fixed lattice enter; it does not explain whether this particular application was later completed.
worth: Worth checking the missing reduction because it controls a concrete finiteness assertion.

title: Are the resulting discrete groups isomorphic?
as_he_states: After asserting finitely many integral fibre functors, ask whether their discrete automorphism groups are all isomorphic up to an unspecified qualification.
plausible_today: For specified integral torsors, compare the integral points of the resulting inner forms; first recover the missing qualification near isomorphes.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne–Milne3.2 identifies torsor twists and inner forms; Borel–Harish-Chandra6.9 gives a finiteness result, not an abstract-group isomorphism theorem for all those forms.
why_open: The qualifier is unreadable and no exact modern assertion can be extracted beyond the comparison question.
worth: Worth an ink check before an arithmetic-group investigation.

title: Hodge and Tate conditional fullness
as_he_states: The proposed realization is fully faithful in virtue of the Hodge and Tate conjectures, with normality of X part of the setup.
plausible_today: For pure homological motives, reduce Hom fullness to algebraicity of the corresponding Hodge or Tate tensors on products and twists; retain the conjectural premise.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne’s absolute-Hodge theorem and Arapura’s abelian-type results concern specified enlarged categories. Tate1966 proves abelian Hom over finite fields and Faltings1983 over number fields; neither is the all-cycle Tate conjecture.
why_open: The author explicitly treats Hodge and Tate as hypotheses; the opened sources do not remove them for algebraic-correspondence motives.
worth: Worth a theorem-by-theorem conditional dictionary, not an unconditional reconstruction claim.

title: Essential image of Hodge realization
as_he_states: Caractériser l’image of the realization into representations with Hodge structure.
plausible_today: Separate full faithfulness from an intrinsic criterion for which polarized tensor representations are geometric.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Milne6.8 proves the integral weight-one equivalence with abelian varieties; Arapura §7 records stronger general motivic fullness questions. Neither Hom fullness nor a Tannakian equivalence with representations identifies the geometric essential image by Hodge data alone.
why_open: The text marks the question with a double question mark; no general criterion was verified in the searched sources.
worth: Worth isolating a low-weight or fixed-family essential image.

title: Conjugate fundamental groups as a test
as_he_states: Analyze Serre’s example of conjugate varieties with nonisomorphic topological fundamental groups.
plausible_today: Identify the exact Serre example before asking which motivic tensor invariants distinguish it; do not replace fundamental groups by cohomology rings.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Charles Theorem1 proves an existential conjugate smooth projective pair with different real cohomology algebras. That is a distinct stronger cohomological witness, not a verification of every detail of the unnamed Serre example.
why_open: The page names Serre but gives no complete reference or construction. The exact historical example remains an external identification task.
worth: Worth locating the original example and comparing its actual realization data.

title: Connected geometric group and real Frobenius
as_he_states: The connected component together with real Frobenius generates the real motivic group and yields the asserted fullness.
plausible_today: Assume an exact quotient by Gal(C/R) and identify its geometric kernel with G^0 under the appropriate absolute-Hodge hypothesis.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Corrected Deligne–Milne6.22(a)/6.23(a), footnote21, restores an omitted absolute-Hodge hypothesis for connectedness;6.25 supplies the abelian-motive case. D6 proves the remaining group-generation implication.
why_open: The published correction documents the missing hypothesis; the all-motives conclusion cannot be read as unconditional.
worth: Worth carrying the correction into every use of real motivic connectedness.

title: Variation from one Hodge fibre
as_he_states: Study how the Hodge structure varies, with a one-fibre rigidity expectation in the surrounding reconstruction argument.
plausible_today: For a smooth proper algebraic family over a reduced connected separated finite-type C-base, use a global flat section or global local-system morphism; an arbitrary local VHS is insufficient.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne4.1.2 and4.1.3.1, printed42, give fixed Hodge type for a global flat section;4.1.3.2,43, extends an abelian-scheme local-system morphism algebraic at one fibre.
why_open: The sources settle these precise geometric versions. General algebraic-cycle statements require separate conjectures, and no historical cause for the broader programme’s incompleteness is stated.
worth: Worth expressing the global algebraic hypotheses explicitly before applying one-fibre rigidity.

title: Moduli maps from one value and monodromy
as_he_states: A map to polarized rigidified motivic moduli is determined by one value and the induced pi_1 map.
plausible_today: For fine moduli of polarized abelian varieties with sufficient level over a reduced connected finite-type C-base, require a global compatible integral H¹ local-system identification and one algebraic fibre isomorphism.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne4.1.3.2 plus Milne14.8 proves the abelian-family reconstruction used in D7. No theorem for arbitrary unspecified motivic moduli follows.
why_open: The broad moduli category is not constructed on the pages. The literature verifies a restricted setting, not the full quantifier.
worth: Worth testing exactly which extra tensors and rigidification are needed for the desired moduli problem.

title: Characterizing motivic moduli by rigidity
as_he_states: Perhaps every variety with the preceding rigidity property is a moduli space of motives of suitable type.
plausible_today: Specify the rigidity property, class of varieties and meaning of moduli, including stack versus fine scheme and level structures.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Milne’s period-domain and abelian-moduli results give important examples, while Arapura constructs motivic sheaves in specified settings. No converse characterization with the page’s quantifiers was found.
why_open: The page says Peut-être and does not state the proposed converse precisely; the searched literature does not identify a single settled theorem.
worth: Worth a formulation exercise only after excluding vacuous rigidity examples.

title: Motivically pointed objects
as_he_states: Introduce motivically pointed objects/fibre data as part of the reconstruction programme.
plausible_today: Distinguish an actual geometric point, a tensor fibre functor and a chosen comparison isomorphism, then define a category of pointed objects.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne–Milne3.2 makes the fibre-functor/torsor distinction precise. The page does not establish that every such point is geometric.
why_open: The construction is exploratory and its full category is not specified; no independent historical explanation is available.
worth: Worth stabilizing notation, with no new classification claim until the objects are fixed.

title: Finite tensor pieces versus one global isomorphism
as_he_states: When does isomorphism of every finite tensor restriction imply isomorphism of the full integral fibre functors?
plausible_today: Treat the tensor-Isom sets as an inverse system and prove compatible nonemptiness using a suitable compactness, lifting or descent theorem.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: EGA8.8.2–8.8.3 handles finite diagrams; Deligne–Milne3.2 handles the comparison torsor. Neither turns separate integral points on all finite restrictions into a compatible integral point without further hypotheses.
why_open: The author distinguishes the finite and global questions explicitly. The missing compatibility is a real logical issue, not resolved by finite spreading.
worth: Worth a precise pro-torsor formulation with the actual transition maps.

title: Spreading the finite motivic comparison
as_he_states: If two places agree on the algebraic part of the field, spread a finite tensor piece and compare by transcendental paths.
plausible_today: For a fixed finite collection of varieties, morphisms and tensor relations over a characteristic-zero field, descend to a suitable finite-type geometrically connected model and identify the required local systems.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: EGA8.8.2–8.8.3 descends finite diagrams;9.7.7 controls geometric connectedness after shrinking. Bakker–Tsimerman Lemmas4.12–4.13 gives a precise related path/Betti comparison for finitely generated regular extensions.
why_open: The integral category and all required tensor data are not fully defined on the leaf; finite descent does not settle global compatibility.
worth: Worth a complete finite-piece proof in one specified motivic category.

title: The countable path tower
as_he_states: For countable k, choose smooth geometrically connected transition models so that path torsors have surjective transitions and a nonempty inverse limit.
plausible_today: Retain the elementary inverse-limit lemma under actual surjectivity, but replace the impossible universal geometric tower by a valid construction under additional hypotheses.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: CL-SA07-134 and D8 refute the asserted tower for an algebraic closure of Qbar(t). EGA finite spreading does not supply it. Bakker–Tsimerman4.12–4.13 treats finitely generated regular extensions, not all countable fields.
why_open: The manuscript supplies no construction of the transition models. The obstruction is proved in this run; it does not refute the final fibre-functor comparison.
worth: Worth finding the exact repair or the missing restriction in the surrounding archive.

title: The uncountable continuation
as_he_states: Si k pas dénombrable, with no surviving completion.
plausible_today: Formulate the comparison for a fixed category over an uncountable field, including the indexing system and the desired compatible paths or torsor point.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Bakker–Tsimerman Proposition4.14 constructs specified rational Nori categories via countable subfields; this is a useful later framework, not a theorem identifying the unfinished integral assertion.
why_open: The sentence ends before a statement is made, so no exact conjecture can be assigned a solved/open fate.
worth: Worth seeking continuation sheets before mathematical development.

title: Separation on the algebraic part
as_he_states: If the places differ on E, some finite tensor subcategory should distinguish their integral Betti functors.
plausible_today: Specify whether places are modulo conjugation, what E is, and whether Hodge data are included; ask separation for those exact equivalence classes.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Charles proves existence of a conjugate pair with different real cohomology rings; it does not separate every prescribed pair of embeddings. The later Hodge-enriched elliptic test has additional hypotheses.
why_open: The page only says je pense, and the deleted reduction does not supply a proof.
worth: Worth first testing the universal quantifier against the real-conjugation identifications already present in the manuscript.

title: Different cohomology rings of conjugate varieties
as_he_states: Find a smooth projective variety whose conjugates have nonisomorphic cohomology rings.
plausible_today: The existential real-cohomology-algebra statement for two embeddings of a number field is precise and established; prescribed-pair separation is stronger.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Charles Theorem1 proves the existential statement; first arXiv circulation25 June2007, publication2009, with both dates checked.
why_open: The source establishes the later result but does not document the fate of every stronger place-separation variant.
worth: Worth a direct historical link; no new proof is needed for the established existential claim.

title: One motive separating archimedean places
as_he_states: For a number field and M sufficiently large, is the map from places into integral Isom-torsor classes injective?
plausible_today: Fix M, its integral tensor category, the quotient on embeddings, and whether Hodge/real data are retained.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Tannakian torsors are established by Deligne–Milne3.2. Charles’s existential example supplies some separating tensors for some pairs, not a uniform theorem for all places of every field.
why_open: The dependence on M and the integral category is not specified; no exact uniform result was verified.
worth: Worth a finite-field-of-definition test with explicit motives and torsors.

title: Which motivic torsors come from places?
as_he_states: Does every principal homogeneous space under the integral motivic group come from an archimedean place, after adding the Riemann–Hodge conditions?
plausible_today: Separate arbitrary torsors from torsors possessing a complex comparison point and an admissible polarized integral Hodge structure.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne–Milne3.2 classifies fibre functors by torsors, not geometric origins. Milne6.8 gives the abelian weight-one essential image only.
why_open: The manuscript itself warns that an unqualified torsor is inadequate and requests extra conditions.
worth: Worth identifying necessary conditions before testing surjectivity.

title: Hodge enrichment and separation of embeddings
as_he_states: What changes if the Hodge structures are retained, after the bare-place conjecture was rejected?
plausible_today: For a category containing all specializations of the explicit elliptic test family, an integral Hodge-preserving comparison over the identity of C separates chosen embeddings.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Milne6.8 identifies integral weight-one Hodge structures with complex abelian varieties; D9 and C01 prove the conditional elliptic test. It does not settle torsor essential-image surjectivity or places modulo conjugation.
why_open: The page explicitly retracts the unfiltered version and proposes the elliptic test rather than a general proof.
worth: Worth formalizing the minimum family-availability and integral hypotheses.

title: Recovering maps from tensor functors
as_he_states: To what extent is a scheme morphism known from its induced contravariant motivic tensor functor?
plausible_today: Specify source, target, motivic category, coefficient and enrichment, then separate faithfulness from characterization of geometric functors.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Tate/Faltings recover Hom of abelian varieties from l-adic modules under their field hypotheses; Mochizuki TheoremA recovers dominant maps to hyperbolic pro-curves from open Galois-compatible group maps over sub-p-adic fields. These are distinct restricted settings, not a universal motivic theorem.
why_open: The manuscript asks an open-ended question; later theorems do not identify its entire domain.
worth: Worth choosing one precise target class and one realization before making a reconstruction conjecture.

title: The immersive moduli criterion
as_he_states: A global polarized motive giving an immersion of Y into moduli should make Y recoverable in the proposed anabelian sense.
plausible_today: State an actual fine moduli map and prove that the tensor functor recovers its image and factorization, not merely the ambient family.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne4.1.3.2 controls abelian families; Milne14.8 gives their Hodge description. Neither theorem alone recognizes an arbitrary subvariety in moduli or every map into it.
why_open: The note is an abbreviated programme without all quantifiers or the needed essential-image statement.
worth: Worth separating family rigidity from recognition of the subvariety.

title: The unclear local true case
as_he_states: An insertion says the assertion is true for an uncertain local k-scheme and refers to a first case.
plausible_today: No precise formulation is justified until the local hypothesis and antecedent are recovered.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: The surrounding Hodge/Tannakian sources explain the context but identify no theorem with the unread condition. This remains classF rather than a manufactured special case.
why_open: The essential words and reference are uncertain in the supplied transcription.
worth: Worth only an ink and continuation check at present.

title: Six conjectural descriptions of motives
as_he_states: Describe motives by six combinations of Betti, de Rham, Hodge, Gauss–Manin, Tate and filtered crystalline data.
plausible_today: Treat each description as a proposed realization category with its own coefficients and admissibility, rather than an asserted equivalence of six unspecified categories.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne–Milne gives abstract tensor reconstruction; Choudhury–Gallauer9.1 compares Nori/Ayoub groups for a fixed embedding and coefficients; Colmez–Fontaine addresses a specified local rational category. None proves the six-fold list as written.
why_open: The heading itself says conjectural and the entries do not state essential-image axioms.
worth: Worth a precise realization-by-realization table before a new theorem is proposed.

title: Missing local analogues of1′ and4′
as_he_states: For p-divisible groups up to isogeny, what replaces the Betti/de Rham and Betti/Gauss–Manin entries?
plausible_today: Fix a mixed-characteristic complete discretely valued field and distinguish rational Tate representations, crystalline modules and Hodge–Tate filtrations; clarify the transcribed l versus p.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Colmez–Fontaine TheoremA supplies rational semistable admissibility; it does not create a literal integral Betti lattice over a p-adic field. Oda concerns characteristic-p H¹ and finite group schemes.
why_open: The page explicitly leaves the two slots empty; a modern analogy is not an exact missing manuscript definition.
worth: Worth reconstructing the local dictionary with all variance and weight conventions.

title: Filtered Frobenius essential image
as_he_states: Which filtered crystalline data arise in the intended p-divisible or pseudo-motivic category?
plausible_today: For rational semistable representations use weakly admissible filtered(phi,N)-modules; impose N=0 for crystalline representations, appropriate two Hodge–Tate weights for p-divisible groups, and lattice conditions for integral models.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Colmez–Fontaine TheoremA proves weakly admissible implies admissible in its rational category. The cited theorem alone does not establish the extra p-divisible or integral equivalence.
why_open: The page does not separate these categories. The established rational theorem is a partial precise fate, not a blanket answer.
worth: Worth documenting the exact narrower p-divisible classification before claiming the local list is solved.

title: Equality of the two modified sections
as_he_states: After modifying two splittings by u and jχ, write that the modified sections agree.
plausible_today: State that equality as an additional comparison compatibility, or prove it from a specified geometric comparison; centralization only ensures each is a homomorphism.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: C05 and D10 give a complete split-extension counterexample to the missing implication. Deligne–Milne torsor formalism does not identify this local extension with an arithmetic motivic exact sequence.
why_open: The page says On écrit que, without deriving the equality from the previous centralization observations.
worth: Worth recovering the intended compatibility datum before using the resulting cocycle formula.

title: The kernel and cyclotomic condition
as_he_states: Infer keru=kerχ∩kerφ from φ=u(jχ)^{-1}.
plausible_today: The equality is valid exactly with the extra implication keru⊆kerχ; otherwise only kerχ∩keru=kerχ∩kerφ follows.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: C06 verifies a counterexample on C₂ and D10 proves the corrected identity. No unseen LM6 A22/A50 statement is assumed to provide the missing premise.
why_open: The needed implication is not written in the supplied passage.
worth: Worth finding the omitted Tate-character hypothesis; the elementary correction is already complete.

title: Integral Chow specialization with torsion
as_he_states: Develop integral Chow-ring specialization compatible with Chern classes, rather than only the rational comparison; the wording is weakened to il semble.
plausible_today: Specify a smooth proper family over a trait and the chosen Chow specialization, then check the integral diagram with torsion and its exact hypotheses.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: SGA6 X7.13.11 is the exact later locator. Original printed579 and581 were viewed, but printed580 is absent from the accessible scan assembly; the integral middle diagram is not independently original-verified in this run.
why_open: The author explicitly says this would require developing specialization. The verification limit here is source access, not evidence that the standard specialization theorem is open.
worth: Worth obtaining the missing original page and matching every arrow before a final historical identification.

title: Tate graded-index consistency
as_he_states: Use the written Tate weight/Hodge shifts together with a possibly unshifted associated-graded expression.
plausible_today: Use Gr_i^W(E(n))=Gr_{i+2n}^W(E)(n); decide on the scan whether the disputed line already says this.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Deligne82 p9 fixes Q(n); C14 verifies the shifts and the pure Tate counterexample to an unshifted reading.
why_open: This is a transcription/index question rather than an unsolved mathematical conjecture.
worth: Worth an ink check because the wrong index propagates into the Hodge torsor construction.

title: Which object is the splitting torsor Q?
as_he_states: Q is called a space of Levi subgroups and also an H′-torsor; the arrows and dimensions are used in the period field diagram.
plausible_today: Distinguish the U-torsor of splittings from an H′-torsor that includes the Tate G_m, and specify any quotient or chosen Tate trivialization.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: The parabolic/Levi dimensions are elementary and C08 checks GL₂: splitting dimension1, H′ dimension2. Deligne–Milne5.1 distinguishes identity-functor central grading from a realization grading.
why_open: The page uses overlapping notation and a reverse forgetful arrow; no opened reference decides its intended convention.
worth: Worth resolving first, since the strong g+u conjecture depends on this dimension.

title: The strong g+u transcendence conjecture
as_he_states: For k⊂Qbar, trdeg_k k(α,β)=dimG+dimU′, with the displayed consequences for α,β,γ and flags.
plausible_today: After fixing Q and all bases, distinguish the ordinary period point from the extra Hodge-splitting coordinates; state field bounds and genericity over the correct base.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Bost–Charles Definition2.9/Conjecture2.12 and KSV2026 separate generated torsors from period genericity. The full non-CM elliptic arithmetic period conjecture is not proved by these results; Bakker–Tsimerman proves a function-field theorem.
why_open: The page states a conjecture, and its Q-dimension ambiguity is an additional formulation problem. No source gives a historical explanation of this exact stronger version.
worth: Worth reconstructing the torsor diagram before comparing it to current period conjectures.

title: The cancelled normalized period draft
as_he_states: After removing the Tate determinant, the only relations should leave dimensiong−1; the elliptic examples and base-field qualification are all cancelled.
plausible_today: Preserve the withdrawn layer; a precise normalized period conjecture needs the determinant relation, square-root field and the intended algebraic or transcendental base.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: C15 verifies determinant normalization only. Grothendieck1966 note10 distinguishes individual transcendence from algebraic independence. The modern period-torsor formulation is in Bost–Charles, not a proof of the cancelled equality.
why_open: The author struck out the entire page; the reason for cancellation is not stated. No reason is invented from later literature.
worth: Worth a historical comparison and an ink check of the undefined normalization symbol, not resurrection as a live theorem.

title: Elliptic full-period degrees four and two
as_he_states: For an elliptic curve over Qbar, ask trdeg Q(α)=4 without CM and2 with CM.
plausible_today: Use the full period/quasiperiod matrix and its Tate determinant, over the algebraic definition field, with the motivic group GL₂ or the CM torus.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: Bost–Charles §2.2 records the CM elliptic period result and the remaining genericity conjecture. KSV5.13 proves a generated de Rham–Betti torsor statement for elliptic products; it does not prove full non-CM transcendence degree4.
why_open: The live page leaves question marks. The known CM result and unresolved full non-CM claim are different fates.
worth: Worth preserving as a central historical period-conjecture formulation, with no claim of a short-run solution.

title: The subgroup generated by the period locus
as_he_states: After translating the algebraic locus of the comparison point to contain1, is its generated algebraic subgroup H equal toG?
plausible_today: Fix Qbar coefficients, the tensor category and the minimal algebraic torsor; distinguish its generated torsor from the raw Zariski closure of the point.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19: KSV2026 Proposition3.1 identifies the minimal generated torsor with the appropriate de Rham–Betti torsor; Theorem5.13 supplies elliptic-product equality under its coefficient hypotheses. It is weaker than full period genericity.
why_open: The manuscript separates this question from transcendence degree. The modern theorem confirms why collapsing them would overstate the result.
worth: Worth an exact notation match to the modern minimal-torsor construction.

title: Algebraic Hodge splitting for a non-CM elliptic curve
